product: NeXT Personal, an ultrasensitive tumor-informed MRD/ctDNA blood test that detects cancer recurrence and monitors therapy response in solid tumors. Q2 2026 delivered 10,384 clinical tests, up 199 percent year over year, with more than 1,400 ordering physicians (2026-08-04 8-K exhibit 99.1). Personalis also sequences samples for the VA Million Veteran Program.
demand: Volume-led now, price later. Clinical volume rose 199 percent year over year and 33 percent sequentially in Q2 2026 (2026-08-04 8-K). Clinical revenue grew 442 percent to $2.6M on new Medicare coverage; pharma and other revenue rose 51 percent to $16.8M; population sequencing (VA MVP) fell 9 percent to $3.0M. Tempus expects ASP lift later (2026-09-15 425).
pricing_power: Gross margin is already thin: Q2 2026 revenue $22.357M against cost of revenue $17.614M, about 21 percent (2026-08-04 8-K exhibit 99.1). Collapse risk from slower specimen receipts, reimbursement or coverage rollback, VA MVP volume shortfall, price competition from Natera and Guardant, and merger costs or a failed close.
competition: Yes, at scale. Natera and Guardant sell competing MRD/ctDNA assays, and Tempus CEO describes ASP convergence toward Natera pricing (2026-09-15 425). Chinese sequencing providers such as BGI and MGI compete on sequencing cost, but no dated evidence shows a low-cost clone matching NeXT Personal sensitivity; treat as context only.
market_strategy: Chris Hall, 2026-07-20: after conducting an exhaustive process, we are confident the Tempus offer provides the most value to our shareholders and the fastest path to bringing our tests to patients (8-K exhibit 99.1). 2026-08-04: we remain firmly on-track to achieve more than a 500 percent increase in our clinical revenue over last year.
bull: Q2 2026 clinical tests up 199% y/y, clinical revenue up 442% to $2.6M, four Medicare indications, and a signed Tempus merger at $16.25 with a rival bidder (8-K 2026-08-04; SEC 425 2026-09-15).
bear: Stock trades at $16.46 above the $16.25 deal price, so the thesis is merger completion, not operations; gross margin is only 21%, and Brodsky & Smith opened merger investigations on 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-23.
falsifier: The Personalis special meeting fails to adopt the Tempus merger, or Tempus Class A closes below $46.00 giving Personalis a termination right (SEC 425, 2026-09-15).
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 30 days: 2026-08-20 new VA MVP task order up to $18.3M effective 2026-09-30 (8-K); 2026-09-09 and 2026-09-23 Brodsky & Smith shareholder investigations of the merger (GlobeNewswire). Last 90 days: 2026-07-20 Tempus AI agreed to acquire Personalis for $16.25 per share, about $1.5B enterprise value (8-K); 2026-08-04 Q2 revenue $22.4M.
web_true_now_not_modelled: Per Tempus CEO Lefkofsky 2026-09-15 (SEC 425), Personalis MRD ASPs will rise above $1,000 versus the roughly $400 per test fee Personalis pays Tempus today, and a rival bidder appeared, accelerating the deal. Medicare coverage now spans four indications (2026-05-19, 2026-08-04). PSNL closed 2026-09-25 at $16.46, above the $16.25 deal price (stockanalysis).
web_demand_product: NeXT Personal, an ultrasensitive tumor-informed MRD/ctDNA blood test that detects cancer recurrence and monitors therapy response in solid tumors. Q2 2026 delivered 10,384 clinical tests, up 199 percent year over year, with more than 1,400 ordering physicians (2026-08-04 8-K exhibit 99.1). Personalis also sequences samples for the VA Million Veteran Program.
web_price_volume_mix: Volume-led now, price later. Clinical volume rose 199 percent year over year and 33 percent sequentially in Q2 2026 (2026-08-04 8-K). Clinical revenue grew 442 percent to $2.6M on new Medicare coverage; pharma and other revenue rose 51 percent to $16.8M; population sequencing (VA MVP) fell 9 percent to $3.0M. Tempus expects ASP lift later (2026-09-15 425).
web_bottleneck: Reimbursement and sample supply. Personalis needed per-indication Medicare coverage, reaching four indications by 2026-08 (8-K 2026-05-19 and 2026-08-04). New VA MVP revenue depends on receiving samples and performing services (8-K 2026-08-20). Tempus CEO cites genetic-counselor scarcity and payer adoption as gating factors (2026-09-15 425).
web_who_benefits_next: Tempus AI (TEM), the acquirer and US distributor; Moderna and Merck via the V940 melanoma sequencing program whose national rollout RFP Tempus won (2026-09-15 425); Tempus oncology network, biopharma data customers, and reference labs. Personalis holders benefit through the 0.3356 exchange ratio and any Tempus cash election up to 50 percent.
web_who_loses: Rival MRD and ctDNA vendors: Natera, Guardant Health, Foundation Medicine and Exact Sciences. Tempus CEO frames Personalis ASPs converging toward Natera pricing and calls MRD a $20B market (2026-07-20 exhibit 99.1; 2026-09-15 425). Tempus itself loses the $400 per test distribution fee once Personalis ASPs exceed it.
web_margin_collapse_risk: Gross margin is already thin: Q2 2026 revenue $22.357M against cost of revenue $17.614M, about 21 percent (2026-08-04 8-K exhibit 99.1). Collapse risk from slower specimen receipts, reimbursement or coverage rollback, VA MVP volume shortfall, price competition from Natera and Guardant, and merger costs or a failed close.
web_low_cost_substitute: Yes, at scale. Natera and Guardant sell competing MRD/ctDNA assays, and Tempus CEO describes ASP convergence toward Natera pricing (2026-09-15 425). Chinese sequencing providers such as BGI and MGI compete on sequencing cost, but no dated evidence shows a low-cost clone matching NeXT Personal sensitivity; treat as context only.
web_ceo_promised: Chris Hall, 2026-07-20: after conducting an exhaustive process, we are confident the Tempus offer provides the most value to our shareholders and the fastest path to bringing our tests to patients (8-K exhibit 99.1). 2026-08-04: we remain firmly on-track to achieve more than a 500 percent increase in our clinical revenue over last year.
web_did_they_deliver: Largely yes so far. 2026-08-04 Q2 2026 revenue $22.4M versus $17.2M, up 30 percent; clinical revenue $2.6M versus $0.5M, up 442 percent; 10,384 clinical tests, up 199 percent year over year; cash $212.7M. Medicare coverage reached four indications (2026-05-19, 2026-08-04). Guidance and earnings calls were discontinued after the 2026-07-20 merger.
web_what_would_falsify: Observable disconfirmers: Tempus Class A stock closing below $46.00, giving Personalis a termination right (2026-09-15 425); the Personalis special meeting failing to adopt the merger; or Q3 2026 results showing clinical test volume or clinical revenue growth stalling, or a Medicare coverage denial for colorectal and other indications.
